To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The band gap and electron mass of H-passiated GNRs can be described within a simple TB model.
edge passivation of GNRs and uniaxially strained GNRs can be described within one model by simply modifying the parameters of the model Hamiltonian.

the energy band gap of H-passivated AGNRS under uniaxially applied strains can be described within a simple model that combines tight-binding (T.B.) approximation with parameters derived form first principle calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of electronic properties of graphene nanoribons (GNRs) under uniaxual strain and the edge passivation of GNRs using the tight-binding model.
the electronic properties of H-passivated AGNRS and their dependence on uniaxial tensile strain.
the influence of uniaxial stress on the electronic structure and the effective mass of hydrogenated armchair graphene nanribbons (AGNR) within the framework of the tight-binding model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

edge passivation is a very efficient way to tune the energy gap and the electron effective mass of AGNRs, while the strain can also be used as an efficient tool to tune the band gap, but the electron effective mass is not so easy to tune by strain.
the band gap is a periodic function of strain and the effective mass is also a periodic function of the same but with a non-linear variation.
the band gap of the H-passivated AGNRS is strongly influenced by strain and the effective mass is strongly influenced by the width of the ribbon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronic properties of graphene nanoribons can be tuned by edge passivation and/or strain.
the energy gap and electron effective masses of H-passivated GNRs can be modulated by strain, and the band gap and effective mass show similar zigzag patterns under strain.
the electronic properties of H-passivated AGNs can be modulated by uniaxial strains and this effect could be described within a TB model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy gap and electron effective masses of AGNRs can be modulated by strain and H-passivation.
the energy gap and the effective mass of AGNRs can be controlled by strain.
a simple model which is computationally efficient and can be easily implemented can capture the essential physics of the problem.
